hook: This rocket engine fired for 500 seconds straight.
narration: This rocket engine fired for eight minutes and twenty seconds without stopping.
It is an RS-25, built to launch NASA's Moon rocket. Four of them fire together at liftoff.
This one was brand new. NASA tested it at Stennis Space Center in Mississippi on November twelfth, 2025.
It ran at up to one hundred and eleven percent power.
The white cloud is mostly steam. The engine burns hydrogen and oxygen, so its exhaust is water.
[short pause] The frost on the pipes comes from fuel colder than four hundred degrees below zero.
outcome: The test ran the full five hundred seconds before the engine shut down.
title: Rocket engine fired for 500 seconds
description:
On Nov. 12, 2025, NASA tested a new production RS-25 engine for the SLS Moon rocket on the Fred Haise Test Stand at Stennis Space Center in Mississippi, firing it for 500 seconds at up to 111% power.
